title: NCEP R1 and R2 used ocean temperatures 0.14-0.23 C too cold from 11 February 2020 and 0.34-0.42 C too cold after 2022 (60S-60N); their 2020-2026 global surface air is 0.16-0.25 C too cold
abstract: Question: do the SST and snow boundary inputs of the NCEP reanalyses agree with independent data in their final years? Over open water, NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1 (R1) uses the SST analysis that it receives as its skin temperature, so R1 ocean skin temperature records the SST input. Approach: we compared R1 and NCEP-DOE R2 ocean skin temperature with five SST products (OI SST v2, DOISST v2.1, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2, ERA5) at 60S-60N, dated changes with 6-hourly R1 files, and measured the effects on 2 m temperature (against ERA5, GHCN-CAMS and Berkeley Earth), turbulent heat fluxes, snow and UAH lower-troposphere temperature. Results: on 11 February 2020 at 06 UTC the R1 SST field changed at 93% of ocean points and its 60S-60N mean fell by 0.21 C in 6 hours; on 7 March 2020 the daily update moved from 12 to 00 UTC. Relative to 2010-2019, R1 minus the references is -0.14 to -0.23 C in March 2020 to August 2022 and, after a drift in September 2022 to January 2023, -0.34 to -0.42 C to February 2026 (largest at 40-60N). R2 has the same errors. In R1 the 2023/24 ocean is 0.18-0.22 C colder than 2015/16, while products show +0.19 to +0.25 C. R1 snow at 40-70N stays too long in spring and summer from 2020 and nearly disappears in winter 2022/23; R1 land 2 m temperature is 0.39-0.47 C too cold (up to -2.2 C in June 2020 at 45-75N). Global 2 m temperature is 0.22-0.25 C (R1) and 0.16-0.23 C (R2) colder than ERA5, so 2016 stays the warmest R1 year. Over 60S-60N ocean, R1 turbulent heat loss falls by 7.2 +/- 1.5 W m-2, a false ocean heat gain. The free troposphere over the ocean has no step against UAH. Consequence: R1 and R2 surface fields from February 2020 to their end are not fit for trends, records or energy budgets without correction. Limitations: the cause and the new input product are not documented; 6-hourly checks cover four years; the flux and snow results have no independent flux or snow reference.
